title: A pilot study to investigate prognostic marker in HPV-induced neoplasia on their way to carcinoma
summary: The cervix carcinoma is the fourth most common cancer for women worldwide. In most cases the disease is caused by a high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) strain. Years of research about these viruses, the carcinoma and a corresponding vaccination were able to force back the cervix carcinoma on rank 11 for cancer of women in germany. But despite the decades of research it remains unclear which tumors will reduce in size over time and which women will need a surgery to prevent an invasive carcinoma. With the stated research project wie want to investigate and characterize in the detail the different grades from a cervix dysplasia to a cervix carcinoma. The aim is to develop prognosis marker which can predict the outcome of a cervix dysplasia more precisely. This could help to decide for a more personal and better therapy option.
conditions: Other noninflammatory disorders of vulva and perineum

interventions.name: patients with CIN (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia) grade I/ VIN grade I/ VAIN grade I
patients with CIN (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia) grade II/ VIN grade II/ VAIN grade II
patients with CIN (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia) grade III// VIN grade III/ VAIN grade III
patients with cervix carcinoma/ vulva carcinoma/ vagina carcinoma

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspicious Pap-result and the patient comes to the dysplasia center of Klinikum Oldenburg for further consultation; abnormal changes in the cervix/vulva/vaginal tissue
Exclusion criteria:
already in chemo-/radiotherapy
